# Model Setup {#sec-setup}

## Environment

There are two players: labor ($L$) and management ($M$). They compete over policy implementation. The winner receives its prize value; the loser receives 0. Contest technology follows @tullock1980. Endogenous timing follows @hamilton1990 and @fu2006.

::: {#def-prizes}
### Asymmetric Prize Values

If labor wins, labor obtains $V_L>0$ and management obtains 0. If management wins, management obtains $V_M\equiv V>0$ and labor obtains 0. Prize values may differ.
:::

## Information Structure

Management knows only the distribution of $V_L$. At the timing stage, labor also has not observed its type. After timing is chosen, labor privately observes $V_L$ and the effort subgame begins. Timing is therefore based on ex ante expected payoffs. Let $V_L$ have support $[\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta]$, with $\mu>\delta>0$, so $\E[V_L]=\mu$.

Define

$$
u_\ell \equiv \sqrt{\mu-\delta}, \qquad
u_H \equiv \sqrt{\mu+\delta}.
$$ {#eq-u-types}

We use two baseline distributions.

::: {#def-binary}
### Binary Distribution {#sec-distributions}

$$
V_L \in \{V_\ell,V_H\}=\{\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta\},
$$

with probability $1/2$ on each type, so $\Var(V_L)=\delta^2$.
:::

::: {#def-uniform}
### Uniform Distribution

$$
V_L \sim U[\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta],
$$

with density $f(v)=1/(2\delta)$, so $\Var(V_L)=\delta^2/3$.
:::

Both distributions share mean $\mu$ and support $[\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta]$, but differ in variance. Equilibrium expressions use three moments:

$$
\kappa \equiv \E\!\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{V_L}}\right],
\qquad
\nu \equiv \E\!\left[\sqrt{V_L}\right],
\qquad
\lambda \equiv \E\!\left[\frac{1}{V_L}\right].
$$ {#eq-moments}

## Timeline

The timing protocol follows the three-stage logic in @fu2006:

1. Stage 0: labor and management simultaneously choose whether to act in period 1 or period 2.
2. Stage 1: nature realizes $V_L$, and only labor observes its realized type.
3. Stage 2: players choose effort in the induced institution SS, ML, or LM.

Type-level payoffs can be compared after realization; timing is chosen ex ante.

::: {#prp-moments}
### Moment Comparison

The moments are:

|  | Binary | Uniform |
|---|---|---|
| $\Var(V_L)$ | $\delta^2$ | $\delta^2/3$ |
| $\kappa$ | $\dfrac{1}{2u_\ell}+\dfrac{1}{2u_H}$ | $\dfrac{u_H-u_\ell}{\delta}$ |
| $\nu$ | $\dfrac{u_\ell+u_H}{2}$ | $\dfrac{u_H^3-u_\ell^3}{3\delta}$ |
| $\lambda$ | $\dfrac{1}{2u_\ell^2}+\dfrac{1}{2u_H^2}$ | $\dfrac{\ln(u_H/u_\ell)}{\delta}$ |

: Key moments under binary and uniform distributions {#tbl-moments}
:::

::: {.proof}
See @sec-proof-moments.
:::

## Contest Payoffs and Best Responses

The Tullock success function is $p_i=x_i/(x_L+x_M)$. Net expected payoffs are

$$
U_L(x_L,x_M;V_L)=\frac{x_L}{x_L+x_M}V_L-x_L,
$$ {#eq-ul}

$$
U_M(x_L,x_M;V)=\frac{x_M}{x_L+x_M}V-x_M.
$$ {#eq-um}

First-order conditions give

$$
x_L^*(x_M;V_L)=\sqrt{V_Lx_M}-x_M,
$$ {#eq-brl}

$$
x_M^*(x_L;V)=\sqrt{Vx_L}-x_L.
$$ {#eq-brm}

Management's best response @eq-brm depends only on effort $x_L$ and known value $V$, not on beliefs. This drives the separation result below.
